### 2026-11-22 Runtime-3.0 CookieStore/CookieJar semantic compatibility audit — decision complete, hidden WebView NO-GO

- **Branch / audited HEAD:** `integration/legado-upstream-runtime` / `a00374e15a0030fd754b83977dd21a4b16689edc`. The latest branch commit list confirms this is the current HEAD. `main` remains `65b1a271a887b494f88c7e09277c5fb9367c6381`. Fixed upstream remains `LegadoTeam/legado@330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **Scope and source inspection:** read-only comparison of pinned `CookieStore.kt`, `CookieManager.kt`, `BackstageWebView.kt`, `JsExtensions.kt`, `AnalyzeUrl.kt`, `WebViewActivity.kt`, `NetworkUtils.kt`, `HttpHelper.kt`, `BaseSource.kt`, `CookieDao.kt`, `Cookie.kt`, and `CookieManagerExtensions.kt`; compared Badcat `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.kt`, `RhinoSourceCookieExtensions.kt`, `BadcatReadingEngineFactory.kt`, `RhinoSourceScriptRuntime.kt`, `SourceRequestFactory.kt`, and `integration-contract/.../OkHttpSourceRequestClient.kt`, plus the current manifest and Cookie helper tests.
- **Pinned Legado ownership and domain semantics:**
  - `NetworkUtils.getSubDomain(url)` uses OkHttp PublicSuffixDatabase effective-TLD-plus-one (eTLD+1), with IP/invalid-host fallback. `CookieStore` is keyed by that registrable-domain string, not by BookSource ID. Different BookSources on the same eTLD+1 therefore intentionally share the same CookieStore state; unrelated registrable domains are separate.
  - Persistent cookies are stored in the Room `cookies` row keyed by the domain string and cached in memory. Session cookies are held separately in `CacheManager` under `${domain}_session_cookie` and are lost on process restart.
  - HTTP `CookieManager.saveCookiesFromHeaders` parses Set-Cookie response headers, separates `persistent` from non-persistent cookies, stores only `name=value` pairs, and merges by cookie name. The resulting CookieStore string does not retain Domain, Path, Expires/Max-Age, Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite attributes. `CookieStore.getCookie(url)` selects by eTLD+1 and merges persistent plus session maps; it does not perform RFC URL path/secure matching.
  - `CookieStore.setCookie(url,cookie)` stores the supplied string under eTLD+1. `replaceCookie` merges incoming name/value pairs over existing pairs rather than replacing the entire set. `removeCookie(url)` deletes the entire eTLD+1 persistent and session store, then expires matching Android WebView cookies for the host and eTLD+1. `CookieStore.clear()` calls `cookieDao.deleteOkHttp()` (rows whose key contains `|`); it is not the same operation as clearing all domain CookieStore rows.
  - `BaseSource.putLoginHeader` extracts the Cookie header and calls `CookieStore.replaceCookie(getKey(), cookie)`; it merges by name. `removeLoginHeader` clears the login header and calls domain-wide `CookieStore.removeCookie(getKey())`.
- **Pinned HTTP request/response callers:**
  - `AnalyzeUrl.setCookie()` merges the CookieStore domain string into the request Cookie header. The `CookieJar` marker is set only when `enabledCookieJar == true`; the pinned model's null value is therefore disabled by this check.
  - `HttpHelper.okHttpClient` has a network interceptor that removes the marker, calls `CookieManager.loadRequest` to merge explicit request cookies with the domain store, then calls `CookieManager.saveResponse` to split persistent/session response cookies. The `OkHttpClient.Builder.cookieJar(cookieJar)` line is commented out in this client; the observed request/response behavior is the explicit interceptor path.
  - Pinned OkHttp follows redirects and SSL redirects. Redirect response Cookie handling must be verified at the exchange level; do not assume the first response is the only cookie write.
- **Badcat production Cookie wiring and differences:**
  - Production wiring is present: `BadcatReadingEngineFactory` supplies source-cookie read/write/replace/remove/login/clear callbacks to `RhinoSourceScriptRuntime` and supplies `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar` to `OkHttpSourceRequestClient`. This is not an unconnected placeholder.
  - Storage is partitioned by `sourceId`, not eTLD+1. Two source IDs on the same registrable domain do not share cookies, unlike Legado. Within one jar, OkHttp's domain/path/secure matching is applied, unlike Legado's domain-wide name/value map.
  - `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.saveFromResponse` persists every cookie with `expiresAt > now`. OkHttp session cookies use the no-expiry sentinel (`Long.MAX_VALUE`), so session cookies are currently persisted and survive process restart. This is a confirmed semantic mismatch. The JSON snapshot retains name/value/domain/path/expiry/hostOnly/secure/HttpOnly, but has no separate session store and does not encode SameSite.
  - `RhinoSourceCookieExtensions.getCookie(url)` returns only cookies matching that exact URL's domain/path/secure rules. `setCookie` parses input as Set-Cookie via `Cookie.parseAll`; pinned `CookieStore.setCookie` stores the supplied name/value string. `replaceCookie(url,...)` removes all cookies applicable to that URL before adding parsed values; pinned replacement merges by name and preserves unrelated names. `removeCookie(url)` removes only URL-applicable cookies in this source jar; pinned removal clears the whole eTLD+1 persistent/session store and matching WebView cookies.
  - Login import differs: Badcat parses raw Cookie pairs into host-only cookies for the exact source host and removes that source-domain family within one sourceId jar. Pinned `putLoginHeader` merges Cookie pairs into the shared eTLD+1 store; pinned logout removes the whole eTLD+1 store, including session state and WebView cookies. Badcat's current source-domain removal preserves unrelated CDN entries and other sourceId jars.
  - `SourceRequestFactory` sets `useCookieJar = source.enabledCookieJar != false`, so null defaults to enabled; pinned `AnalyzeUrl` uses `enabledCookieJar == true`, so null defaults to disabled. Badcat's OkHttp CookieJar is per sourceId and uses OkHttp redirect handling; it deliberately disables HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect following, whereas pinned HttpHelper enables SSL redirects. This security-policy difference must remain explicit rather than silently described as parity.
  - Existing `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJarTest` covers helper-level URL matching, host-only/domain matching, login-pair parsing and source-domain predicates. It does not exercise actual SharedPreferences persistence/restart, session-cookie expiry, same-eTLD+1 sharing across source IDs, HTTP redirect chains, parallel cookie writes, logout side effects, or WebView/subresource behavior.
- **Hidden and visible WebView write owners:**
  - Pinned `AnalyzeUrl` calls `BackstageWebView` with the source key/tag and source header map. Hidden `BackstageWebView` uses `android.webkit.CookieManager.getInstance()`; on page finish it asynchronously reads `getCookie(finalUrl)` and calls `CookieStore.setCookie(sourceTag,cookieString)`. It does not call `CookieManager.applyToWebView()` before its load. The captured string is name/value-only and is stored under the source key's eTLD+1, even when the loaded/final URL is another host.
  - Pinned foreground `WebViewActivity` calls `applyToWebView(url)`, which obtains the process-wide Android WebView CookieManager, removes session cookies globally, and injects CookieStore pairs for the target base URL. On page finish it reads the global CookieManager and writes the result back through `CookieStore.setCookie(url,...)`. Pinned hidden and visible WebViews therefore share a process-wide WebView cookie manager; foreground preparation can clear session cookies used by hidden work.
  - Android `CookieManager.getCookie(url)` returns a request-cookie string, not the original Set-Cookie attributes. A WebView capture/replay bridge cannot claim exact attribute round-trip from that API alone.
  - Badcat's current app manifest declares no dedicated WebView process and no `android:process` component boundary. Its visible/product WebView and any future hidden WebView in the default process would share the same Android WebView CookieManager.
- **Compatibility/security decision:**
  - Do not attach the current sourceId-scoped `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar` directly to a production hidden WebView and call it Legado-compatible. It differs in ownership, default enablement, session persistence, path/domain matching, replacement/removal and login/logout semantics.
  - To match the pinned behavior, the HTTP/JS compatibility layer must use eTLD+1 ownership (including intentional sharing by sources on the same eTLD+1), separate persistent and process-memory session stores, name-based merge semantics, and the pinned null/false `enabledCookieJar` default. Source identity can remain in diagnostics/call context, but cannot silently partition the CookieStore if full parity is the target. If stricter sourceId isolation is chosen instead, it is an explicit compatibility fork and must not be labelled full Legado parity.
  - **A dedicated hidden-WebView Android process and its own WebView data-directory suffix are required** to prevent foreground `applyToWebView()` / global session-cookie clearing from mutating hidden WebView state. The suffix must be established before any WebView/provider initialization (API 28+). A same-process mutex is insufficient because the CookieManager itself is process-global.
  - A dedicated process alone is not sufficient: it still has one process-global CookieManager shared by all hidden WebViews. The design must define per-domain ownership, same-domain concurrent operation behavior, cookie import/export and writeback, and how the authoritative persistent/session CookieStore is accessed across processes. Do not use multi-process SharedPreferences as an implicit synchronization mechanism. Use the typed Host Port/IPC boundary and a single explicit CookieStore owner; prove subresource and redirect behavior before implementation.
  - The upstream WebView cookie bridge is intrinsically lossy for cookie attributes. The implementation must document and test the exact upstream-equivalent name/value behavior; it must not claim preservation of Set-Cookie attributes that WebView `getCookie()` cannot return.
- **Required executable test matrix before hidden WebView GO:**
  1. Two source IDs on the same eTLD+1 share the same persistent and session cookie names/values; different eTLD+1 domains remain isolated.
  2. Same eTLD+1 cookies set on different URL paths are visible according to pinned domain-map semantics; compare against Badcat's current stricter path matching.
  3. Persistent cookies survive process restart; session cookies disappear after process restart; session cookies override same-name persistent entries only as the pinned merge order specifies.
  4. Multiple Set-Cookie headers, same-name updates, empty/invalid values, explicit Cookie header precedence, and JS set/replace/remove/get are differential-tested.

### 2026-11-22 Runtime-3.0 hidden WebView platform floor — user decision accepted

- **Decision owner / approval:** the user explicitly accepted raising the minimum Android version from Android 8.0 / API 26 to Android 9.0 / API 28 on 2026-11-22. This is an approved product compatibility change, not an inferred technical preference.
- **Reason:** Android's `WebView.setDataDirectorySuffix()` is available from API 28. A dedicated hidden-WebView process needs its own WebView data directory before any WebView/provider initialization; the visible Badcat WebView must remain in the default app process and must not share the hidden process's process-global `CookieManager`. API 26/27 cannot satisfy this selected isolation design through the supported suffix API.
- **Current task scope:** change only the app's `defaultConfig.minSdk` from 26 to 28 and record this approved platform floor. The Android library modules may retain minSdk 26 because an app with minSdk 28 can consume them; do not mechanically raise every module.
- **Starting state:** branch `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`, HEAD `5049cef0793ec3b1f81d23fef47862fceec04d6d`; pinned Legado remains `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`. `main` was rechecked at `65b1a271a887b494f88c7e09277c5fb9367c6381` and is not a target.
- **Architecture decision for the next separately scoped implementation task:**
  1. Add a custom `Application` and set the hidden process WebView data-directory suffix in `attachBaseContext`, before provider or application initialization can create a WebView. Confirm merged-manifest providers/startup initializers and fail closed if the suffix cannot be established.
  2. Declare a non-exported Android service in `:legado_hidden_webview`; all WebView creation, navigation, JavaScript evaluation, callbacks and destruction stay on that process's main looper. The foreground/product WebView remains in the default process.
  3. Keep the existing HTTP/JS CookieStore authoritative in the default app process. The hidden process must use an explicit typed IPC boundary for any CookieStore read/write required by the pinned bridge; do not share/mutate the same SharedPreferences file from two processes and do not treat multi-process SharedPreferences as synchronization.
  4. Use explicit Parcelable/AIDL request, result and callback DTOs (or an equivalently typed Binder protocol); carry operation ID and source/caller context, support cancellation, timeout, service death/rebind, bounded pending work and deterministic WebView recycle. Do not serialize coroutine Job or Activity/View references across IPC.
  5. Preserve the pinned WebView cookie bridge's actual name/value-only capture semantics; do not claim Set-Cookie attribute round-trip. Verify subresource, redirect, cache-first, cookie writeback and process-restart behavior before calling the bridge compatible.
  6. Keep visible browser verification, foreground WebView and Badcat product UI distinct from hidden/background WebView execution. No Legado UI/Reader substitution.
- **Pre-implementation audit still required:** inspect all merged-manifest ContentProvider/AndroidX Startup initializers and their process placement; enumerate all WebView/JS callers and lifecycle owners; inspect the existing typed `HiddenWebViewPort` contract and define the Android adapter/IPC mapping; specify CookieStore authority and failure behavior. No production WebView implementation is authorized by the minSdk-only commit.
- **Explicit exclusions:** no Fourth-category source/test/production change; Fourth-category tests remain excluded from Third-category CI until the user asks to validate Fourth-category. No AdMark repair, no UI/Reader redesign, no database/schema migration, no PPRule, no upstream pin change and no `main` modification.
- **Acceptance for this platform-floor task:** inspect the Gradle diff; exact-HEAD CI must compile and pass the Third-category test profile; verify the app manifest/build metadata reports minSdk 28. This does not count as hidden WebView implementation or runtime acceptance.
- **Status at registration:** user decision accepted; app minSdk floor updated in this commit; CI verification pending; hidden process/Application/IPC/WebView implementation remains a separate not-started task.
- **Checklist self-review:** this entry records the user-approved API 28 platform floor and defines the next bounded hidden-process task. No Fourth-category test or source is included.

### 2026-11-22 Runtime-3.1 hidden WebView host/IPC architecture audit — completed

- **Audit source HEAD:** `d60e217bb6a25b53d644ea7c84fde51857f35041` on `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`; the audit is read-only. The result was written at documentation HEAD `3efd492d95cfcd6deb4e5f43e3fa7093aae3d27e`. `main` remains `65b1a271a887b494f88c7e09277c5fb9367c6381`.
- **Merged manifest evidence:** decoded the compiled Debug APK from CI #3131 artifact `14742025590` (same source HEAD `d60e217...`). Its merged `AndroidManifest.xml` reports minSdk 28 / targetSdk 36; the application has no `android:name` custom Application; no service entries; and one provider, `androidx.startup.InitializationProvider`, with metadata `okhttp3.internal.platform.PlatformInitializer`. The provider has no explicit `android:process`, so it belongs to the default app process. No WebView initializer was identified in the merged provider metadata. The host source manifest likewise declares no Application, service, provider or process boundary. Android creates/attaches the process Application before installing that process's ContentProviders; therefore the selected hidden-process suffix belongs in the new host Application's `attachBaseContext`, before provider/application initialization. Do not merge the pinned upstream app manifest wholesale: it brings the upstream `.App`, `ReaderProvider`, `FileProvider` and many unrelated product components.
- **Application/process plan:** introduce a minimal Badcat host Application (not the pinned upstream full `App`) and compare `Application.getProcessName()` against the exact private process name. Only in `:legado_hidden_webview`, call `WebView.setDataDirectorySuffix("legado_hidden_webview")` before `super.attachBaseContext`/any WebView provider use; do not call it in the default process. If suffix setup fails, fail process startup rather than silently creating a WebView in the shared default data directory. Keep Application static initialization free of WebView creation. API 28 is the minimum, so `Application.getProcessName` and `setDataDirectorySuffix` are available.
- **Pinned hidden-WebView call matrix:** at Legado SHA `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`, `JsExtensions.webView` has 3/4-argument overloads; `webViewGetSource` and `webViewGetOverrideUrl` each have 4/5/6-argument overloads. All require a background caller and synchronously await `BackstageWebView.getStrResponse`. They map to `HiddenWebViewOperation.EVALUATE_PAGE`, `CAPTURE_RESOURCE_URL`, and `CAPTURE_OVERRIDE_URL`. Request semantics include URL or HTML/base URL, JavaScript, request headers, User-Agent, cache-first, regex capture, delay, redirects and timeout.
- **Pinned hidden-WebView lifecycle:** `BackstageWebView` posts creation/navigation/evaluation/destruction to the main looper; default timeout is 60 seconds; coroutine cancellation posts destruction; page-finish evaluates JS (with retries); resource capture occurs in `onLoadResource`; override capture occurs in `shouldOverrideUrlLoading`; cookie capture occurs after page finish. `WebViewPool` is a process-local singleton, and `forBackground=true` selects WebViews that have never been attached to a window. It still creates ordinary WebView instances on the main looper; it is not a separate Android process. Release stops loading, removes registered JS interfaces, resets state, navigates to a unique blank URL, and only then returns the view to the idle pool. Idle cleanup destroys expired views. Upstream regression tests cover interface removal, idempotent release, cancellation/stale callback isolation, and resource/override URL capture. The upstream instrumentation lifecycle test currently has an SDK 29 minimum; our API 28 implementation needs its own API 28 coverage.
- **Current host gap:** `RuntimeHostPort.kt` already declares `HiddenWebViewPort`, request/result types and operation IDs, but no production Android service/adapter is wired. `SourceExecutionContext.coroutineJob` and `HostPortError.cause: Throwable?` must not cross Binder. Kotlin `Map`, sealed result objects and platform-neutral context types also need explicit Parcelable/AIDL mapping. The Binder DTO must carry source identity, caller kind, operation ID, navigation policy, operation, URL/HTML/JS, bounded header pairs, cache policy, regex, delay and timeout; return a typed result/error code/message; and expose cancellation by operation ID. Never parcel a `Job`, `Throwable`, Activity, View or WebView.
- **Visible/product UI separation:** pinned `startBrowser` / `startBrowserAwait` route through `SourceVerificationHelp` to visible `WebViewActivity`; `showBrowser` uses visible `BottomWebViewDialog`; `getVerificationCode` uses `VerificationCodeActivity`; `openUrl` and `openVideoPlayer` are product UI actions. `SourceVerificationHelp` owns in-memory verification attempts/flight coordination and must stay in the default process. `SourceLoginJsExtensions.showBrowser` overrides the base action and carries login-specific custom-button state. Existing `HostUiAction.ShowBrowserDialog` currently lacks the login `bookType` / `customButtonKey` data or a local lookup token; extend its host-side mapping without passing Activity/Fragment references.
- **Async JS bridge:** pinned `WebJsExtensions.request` dispatches `webViewAwait` and `webViewGetSourceAwait` from the visible page's JS bridge using callback IDs, then calls `evaluateJavascript` on the original visible WebView. The visible WebView and its callback map remain in the default process; only the hidden operation crosses Binder. When the activity lifecycle cancels, cancel the remote operation and do not leave a JS Promise hanging.
- **Badcat foreground WebViews:** `SourceChapterActivity` owns the reader body/scroll WebViews; `ReaderCssActivity` owns CSS preview WebViews. They are Badcat product UI and must remain in the default process. The hidden service must never return a WebView/View across IPC or replace the reader with Legado UI.
- **Cookie ownership finding — critical design gap:** pinned Legado has two related but distinct stores: its app CookieStore/HTTP persistence and the process-global Android `CookieManager`. `BackstageWebView` reads `CookieManager.getCookie(url)` after page finish and writes the name/value string to `CookieStore.setCookie`; visible `WebViewActivity` applies CookieStore values into its process CookieManager; visible `BottomWebViewDialog` also reads/writes Android CookieManager directly while proxying page requests through OkHttp. Thus login/browser cookies may exist in the default process WebView CookieManager even when they are not yet in the HTTP/JS CookieStore. A hidden process with its own WebView data directory cannot see those cookies. A CookieStore-only IPC snapshot is insufficient.
- **Cookie IPC requirement:** keep all authoritative storage access in the default process. Add a main-process CookieBridge that coordinates both the existing HTTP/JS `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar` (including process-memory session values) and the default-process Android CookieManager. Hidden process must never open the CookieStore SharedPreferences or session map directly. Define explicit bounded cookie snapshot, writeback and domain invalidation messages; synchronize before hidden navigation, await WebView `setCookie` callbacks, capture after page/redirect completion, and propagate logout/remove to the hidden mirror. Track registrable domains encountered by main/hidden WebViews so cross-domain subresource cookies are not silently omitted; a single top-level URL header does not prove cross-domain parity. `CookieManager.getCookie` returns name=value pairs without Set-Cookie attributes, and the pinned CookieStore itself uses name/value map semantics. The current host adapter has process-local locks/session memory and no all-domain snapshot API, so it cannot be accessed as a multi-process store or treated as ready-made IPC.
- **Lifecycle/security protocol:** use a non-exported service in `:legado_hidden_webview` (same app UID; not `isolatedProcess`). All WebView work and callbacks run on that process's main looper; Binder entry points only validate/enqueue and return. Bound pending work and active WebViews; enforce per-operation timeout and cancel; on Binder death/service process death fail every pending operation as interrupted and do not blindly replay non-idempotent navigations. Rebind for future requests. Bound URL/HTML/JS/header/regex/queue sizes to protect Binder and WebView memory. Preserve source/caller identity and navigation policy. Validate schemes and never expose the service to other apps. Upstream `BackstageWebView` currently calls `SslErrorHandler.proceed()` for owned WebViews; this is a known security-sensitive upstream behavior and must be explicitly reviewed rather than copied silently. WebView JS interfaces must be attached only on the pinned paths that require them and removed before pool reuse.
- **Focused acceptance matrix:** API 28 emulator plus API 35 emulator; prove the hidden process has a distinct data directory and default reader still uses the default directory; prove no WebView is created before suffix initialization; bind/unbind/rebind and Binder death; every hidden operation with URL/HTML, headers/UA, cache-first, JS result, resource regex, override regex and redirect; main-looper ownership; timeout/cancel/recycle/stale callback isolation; JS interface removal; bounded concurrency; CookieStore + visible CookieManager snapshot, login-dialog cookies, cross-domain subresources, redirects, cookie writeback, logout/remove invalidation, session/persistent behavior and process restart; ensure visible browser verification and Badcat reader/CSS preview remain in the default process. Verify all three Fourth-category test classes remain excluded from this Third-category lane.
- **Audit conclusion:** architecture is feasible at API 28, and the typed host-port contract is a usable seam, but production implementation is blocked on the dual-store/cross-domain CookieBridge design and the missing login-dialog metadata in `ShowBrowserDialog`. Do not implement a simplistic target-URL-only cookie copy and claim full Legado compatibility.
- **Fourth-category boundary:** no Fourth-category source or test file was inspected for this audit's implementation work, modified or added. Its three test classes remain excluded; no Fourth-category pass is claimed.

#### Runtime-3.2a CookieStore / foreground WebView ownership audit

#### Runtime-3.2a login-dialog metadata and action-context audit

- **Status:** read-only audit complete; no production or test source changed. Audit start HEAD: `0deab7b6545d4a19786b444abac36f645f6867bf`. Branch: `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`. Pinned upstream: `LegadoTeam/legado@330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`. `main` verified unchanged at `65b1a271a887b494f88c7e09277c5fb9367c6381`.
- **Upstream row contract:** pinned `data/entities/rule/RowUi.kt` defines six row types (`text`, `password`, `button`, `label`, `toggle`, `select`) and fields `name/type/action/chars/default/viewName/style/key/hint/value/options/countdown`. `LoginUiV2.parseRender` accepts the same six types; its action result is `state/error/login/close`. `SourceLoginV2Delegate` maps text/password/select/toggle/button/label; button invokes the named action and applies the optional countdown. Toggle may also dispatch an action. These are row/action semantics, not book-type metadata.
- **Legacy login UI behavior is materially broader:** pinned `SourceLoginDialog.handleButtonClick` treats an absolute URL as an external open; otherwise evaluates the legacy login script with `java`, `result`, `book`, `chapter`, and `isLongClick`. It supports long-press distinction for legacy buttons and passes `SourceLoginJsExtensions` into the script. That extension carries `bookType`, `customButtonKey`, and can open `BottomWebViewDialog`. This legacy behavior is not represented by the Login UI v2 row/action schema.
- **Book type semantics:** pinned `BookType` is a bitmask, not a login row enum: video=4, text=8, audio=32, image=64, webFile=128 (with other non-login/local flags). `SourceLoginViewModel` resolves active text/audio/video book and chapter context from the incoming type. `RssJsExtensions.open("login")` forwards the current book type only when routing back to the same BookSource; cross-source and RSS routes do not inherit it. `SourceLoginJsExtensions` forwards it to browser UI configuration. It must remain a typed invocation-context field, never be guessed from sourceType or inserted into a row.
- **Two similarly named custom-button concepts must not be conflated:** upstream `BookSource.customButton` is a source-level Boolean (“由书源控制的自定义按钮”); the existing source codec preserves that field and raw JSON. Separately, `SourceLoginJsExtensions.customButtonKey` identifies/deduplicates a particular browser dialog initiated from a legacy login action. Neither is a Login UI v2 `button.action` identifier.
- **Current Badcat mapping:** `LegadoLoginUiV2.Row` carries row type, key, action, hint, value, options and countdown; `LegadoSourceLoginUiV2Service` evaluates only the V2 `loginUi(state)` / `loginAction(action,state,form)` functions. `SourceLoginUiV2Activity` dispatches the action string and persists state/login JSON. `SourceCatalogActivity` launches it with only source ID, so the current invocation has no bookType/book/chapter context. The script runtime does not provide the legacy `java` browser extension or `isLongClick` callback in this V2 action contract. The activity therefore supports declarative V2 forms only; it does not implement the pinned legacy login dialog.

#### Runtime-3.2c pinned SSL-error callback semantics audit — complete, security blocker recorded

- **Status:** read-only source/caller audit complete; no production or test source changed. Audit start HEAD: `a9a2ce75f8c790637f86b1a8265a9b9ac00af361`; branch: `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`; fixed upstream: `LegadoTeam/legado@330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **Pinned upstream WebView callback inventory:** code search at the pinned SHA found six `onReceivedSslError` overrides in five files: `help/http/BackstageWebView.kt` (both `HtmlWebViewClient` and `SnifferWebClient`, lines 242-253 and 390-401); `ui/login/WebViewLoginFragment.kt` (141-148); `ui/browser/WebViewActivity.kt` (570-577); `ui/widget/dialog/BottomWebViewDialog.kt` (1232-1237); and `ui/rss/read/ReadRssActivity.kt` (913-918). The four visible callbacks call `handler?.proceed()` unconditionally. They do not inspect the `SslError`, distinguish certificate failure kinds, request user consent, or provide a source-specific trust decision.
- **Background source-rule WebView path:** `BackstageWebView.getStrResponse` wraps work in `withTimeout(timeout ?: 60000L)`; coroutine cancellation schedules `destroy()` on the UI thread, which releases the pooled WebView. Both WebView clients use `ownsWebView(view, navigationContext)` (active coroutine plus exact pooled instance) as a stale-owner guard: active owner => `handler?.proceed()`; stale/missing owner => `handler?.cancel()`. This guard prevents a stale operation from proceeding but does not validate the certificate or authorize a user decision. No SSL-specific typed failure is produced in this class; cancellation is not explicitly mapped to a source-engine certificate error.
- **Background callers:** `model/analyzeRule/AnalyzeUrl.kt` lines 482-517 routes `useWebView` requests through `BackstageWebView` (including direct GET and POST-response HTML branches); `model/analyzeRule/AnalyzeRule.kt` lines 183-194 uses it for `webJs`; `help/JsExtensions.kt` lines 291-305, 317-340 and 352-374 expose `java.webView`, `webViewGetSource` and `webViewGetOverrideUrl`. These are the source-rule/runtime-relevant background callers.
- **Visible callers:** `ui/login/SourceLoginActivity.kt` lines 26-33 selects `WebViewLoginFragment` for sources without a declarative login form; that fragment uses a pooled WebView and unconditionally proceeds on SSL errors. `WebViewActivity` and `BottomWebViewDialog` are visible browser paths and also unconditionally proceed. `ReadRssActivity` does the same in the upstream RSS product path; it is recorded as an upstream callsite but does not authorize adding RSS UI to Badcat.
- **Separate upstream HTTP/JS TLS policy:** `help/http/SSLHelper.kt` lines 27-70 defines an `X509TrustManager` whose trust checks are no-ops, an `unsafeSSLSocketFactory`, and a `HostnameVerifier` that always returns true. `help/http/HttpHelper.kt` lines 51-69 installs the unsafe socket factory/trust manager and permissive hostname verifier in the shared OkHttp client, and enables `followSslRedirects(true)`; `AnalyzeUrl.getClient` derives request clients from that shared client. `help/JsExtensions.kt` lines 580-640 uses the unsafe socket factory for JS `get/head/post` Jsoup calls (no explicit permissive hostname verifier in those calls). `help/http/ObsoleteUrlFactory.kt` lines 984-991 supplies the unsafe trust manager when setting a custom socket factory. The pinned source therefore has a broad legacy TLS-bypass behavior, not just WebView callback behavior. `SSLHelper` also contains configurable trust-manager/certificate helpers, but the shared default HTTP client chooses the unsafe path.
- **Badcat comparison:** `integration-contract/src/main/kotlin/app/badcat/engine/OkHttpSourceRequestClient.kt` lines 204-245 uses the default OkHttp TLS trust configuration (no custom trust manager or hostname verifier) and explicitly disables HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect following. `RuntimeHostPort.kt` defines `HiddenWebViewPort` and `VisibleBrowserPort` but no typed SSL-error input, decision, or certificate-failure result. Current `SourceBookActivity.kt` reader WebView loads generated local chapter HTML via `loadDataWithBaseURL`, with JavaScript/DOM storage/file/content access disabled; its WebViewClient only handles `onPageFinished`. It is not the remote source-browser/login WebView and must not be repurposed as one.
- **Security decision / compatibility impact:** do **not** copy the upstream unconditional `proceed()`, trust-all manager, permissive hostname verifier, or HTTPS-downgrade behavior into Badcat. The safe default for any future source WebView host is to cancel every certificate validation error and surface a typed SSL/certificate failure to the calling source operation. A future explicit user override, if ever approved, must be a separate, clearly disclosed, narrowly host-bound one-shot consent flow; it must never be implicit, global, persisted as a trust-all switch, or applied to unrelated subresources. This is an intentional security deviation from pinned Legado behavior; sources that depend on invalid/self-signed certificates may fail until a separately reviewed consent design exists. Do not claim complete upstream SSL parity.
- **Required focused test matrix for the future host adapter:** trusted certificate success; untrusted/self-signed, expired, not-yet-valid and hostname-mismatch certificate errors cancel; null handler/error fails closed without crash; stale WebView/cancelled coroutine cancels; redirect and subresource callback handling follows the same deny policy; cancellation/timeout race completes once and releases the WebView; certificate failure returns a typed engine/host error rather than waiting for the generic 60-second timeout. No test may assert `proceed()` for a certificate error under the default policy.
- **Scope / exclusions:** no source, test, Gradle, manifest, UI, CookieBridge, process/Service/Binder/IPC, Fourth-category source/tests/coordinator, PPRule, schema, upstream pin or `main` changes. Audit evidence is limited to the fixed upstream SHA and current Badcat branch files.
- **Checklist self-review:** enumerated both BackstageWebView client overrides and all visible upstream overrides; followed the source-rule callsites; separated WebView SSL callbacks from OkHttp/Jsoup TLS behavior; verified the current Badcat reader is local-content rendering and current OkHttp host defaults; recorded the explicit security/compatibility conflict. This is an audit, not an implemented SSL adapter.

#### Runtime-3.2e.2 WebView Cookie header import must not promote session cookies — preregistration

- **Status:** registered; implementation not started. Start HEAD: `2897dbc6a366d7643eec03c2e4f5e5d330187f2b`; fixed Legado SHA: `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **Audit evidence:** pinned upstream `app/src/main/java/io/legado/app/help/http/CookieManager.kt` splits response cookies by `Cookie.persistent`: non-persistent values go to the in-memory `<domain>_session_cookie` bucket; persistent values go through `CookieStore.replaceCookie`. `CookieStore.getCookie` merges persistent then session maps, with session values overriding same-name persistent values. Pinned `CookieStore.setWebCookie` / `CookieManager.applyToWebView` write name/value pairs into Android CookieManager without preserving Set-Cookie attributes. Current Badcat `DefaultProcessCookieBridge.syncFromWebView` calls `mergeLoginCookieHeader`, which unconditionally merges the WebView-visible header into SharedPreferences persistence. Android `CookieManager.getCookie(url)` exposes only name/value pairs, not persistence attributes; therefore the bridge cannot safely infer that an imported pair is persistent.
- **Goal:** make WebView-visible Cookie header import conservative and session-scoped. Never promote an unclassified WebView cookie to durable SharedPreferences storage. Preserve existing persistent values; in-process session values must retain the upstream merge precedence (session overrides persistent). When an imported pair equals its persistent value, avoid creating a redundant session override; when it differs, record it only in the session map. This is intentionally conservative because CookieManager does not expose expiry/Max-Age metadata.
- **Allowed production files:** `app/src/main/java/app/badcat/client/runtime/DefaultProcessCookieBridge.kt`; `app/src/main/java/app/badcat/client/runtime/SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.kt`.
- **Allowed tests:** `app/src/test/kotlin/app/badcat/client/runtime/DefaultProcessCookieBridgeTest.kt`; `app/src/test/kotlin/app/badcat/client/runtime/SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJarTest.kt`. No new instrumentation or factory wiring in this task.
- **Required behavior:** WebView import updates only the in-memory session domain map; it never writes imported values to persistent preferences. Persistent values remain unchanged. A differing WebView value for a persistent name shadows it only for the current process; after session-store recreation the prior persistent value is visible again. An imported name/value identical to the persistent value must not become a durable write or unnecessary session override. Existing session/persistent same-name precedence remains deterministic. No cookie values/headers in logs.
- **Focused tests:** (1) imported WebView-only name is visible in current process and absent after session-store recreation; (2) imported value differing from a persistent same-name cookie overrides it in-process but does not overwrite persistence; (3) identical persistent pair does not create a session override; (4) ordinary HTTP response persistence/session classification remains unchanged; (5) existing merge and domain isolation tests continue to pass. Run focused CookieBridge and CookieJar tests, then complete third-category app JVM suite at exact HEAD.
- **Caller inventory / integration boundary:** inspected `DefaultProcessCookieBridge.syncFromWebView`, `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.mergeLoginCookieHeader`, and `BadcatSourceHttpGatewayFactory`; the factory does not instantiate or wire this bridge. Repository code-search returned no indexed external callers for the bridge symbol, so do not claim production runtime integration or expand this task to add it. Recheck all source references at implementation HEAD before editing.
- **Explicit exclusions:** no hidden WebView process/Service/Binder/IPC; no CookieManager provider adapter or API 28/35 platform claim; no invalidation ordering/readback/result changes; no login UI, SSL callback adapter/trust override, factory/service graph wiring, Fourth-category code/tests/coordinator, PPRule, schema, upstream pin or `main`.
- **Exit condition:** if the name/value-only WebView API cannot support the stated conservative session classification without changing upstream persistent/session semantics, stop and document the limitation rather than guessing cookie expiry or promoting values to durable storage.

#### Runtime-3.2e.3 scoped CookieBridge invalidation must verify before clearing the authoritative store — preregistration
- **Failure follow-up evidence (CI #3151, run `45044912933`, exact HEAD `914bbcd26a0716a4901fd0371b00483250e544e2`):** the missing `assertEquals` import was corrected and the production-bridge test executed on API 28 and API 35. This points to a WebView callback thread/Looper-affinity defect; treat that as a hypothesis until verified by dispatching the provider operation through the main Looper and rerunning both providers. Keep the invalidation fail-closed behavior; do not weaken the assertion or clear the store on failure.


- **Status:** registered; implementation not started. Registration base HEAD: `be4582358dcb98687487db08631a2f2508a2fc8f`; fixed Legado SHA: `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`.
- **Audit evidence:** current `DefaultProcessCookieBridge.invalidateDomain` collects names from the authoritative store and observed WebView URLs, issues bounded host/domain/path expiry callbacks and flushes, but then calls `store.removeCookie(sourceUrl)` before readback. It subsequently verifies only WebView names. Thus a provider that accepts a callback but retains a cookie can cause the authoritative domain bucket to be erased while WebView state remains; the current `CookieBridgeInvalidationResult.cleared` Boolean does not expose a typed failure reason or authoritative-store readback.
- **Goal:** make scoped logout/removal fail closed across both stores. Do not clear the authoritative persistent/session bucket until every targeted expiry callback has completed and every target WebView URL reads back with no target cookie names. After WebView verification succeeds, clear the authoritative domain bucket and verify its readback for every target URL. Return a typed success or typed failure with bounded counts, failure category and remaining cookie **names only** (never values or headers). Preserve unrelated registrable domains and propagate caller coroutine cancellation rather than converting it to a cookie success/failure.
- **Allowed production file:** only `app/src/main/java/app/badcat/client/runtime/DefaultProcessCookieBridge.kt`. Reuse existing `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.getCookie/removeCookie`; do not widen the storage API unless source review proves it necessary and the registration is amended first.

- **Required behavior:** (1) provider callback rejection/timeout yields a typed unsuccessful result and preserves authoritative persistent/session data; (2) callbacks that report acceptance while a target cookie remains are detected by per-target-URL WebView readback and do not clear the authoritative bucket; (3) only a fully clean WebView readback permits authoritative removal; (4) authoritative-store readback is checked after removal and any residue is reported as typed failure; (5) success means both stores are verified empty for the bounded target URLs; (6) unrelated registrable domains remain intact; (7) no `removeAllCookies` or global clear; (8) cancellation remains cancellation, not a result value.
- **Typed result contract:** replace the Boolean-only result with a closed success/failure shape. Failure categories must distinguish at least callback rejection, callback timeout, WebView residue, and authoritative-store residue. Result metadata may include tracked URL count, attempted expiry count and maps of remaining names by URL, but must not contain cookie values, raw headers, Android platform objects or unbounded exception text.
- **Focused JVM tests:** callback rejection preserves the store; callback timeout preserves the store; accepted-but-ineffective expiry produces a WebView-residue failure and preserves the store; successful expiry clears both stores; authoritative readback is represented in the result; unrelated-domain preservation remains asserted; cancellation is not swallowed. Keep all existing domain/path/name precedence assertions.

The current workflow already runs `:app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` on API 28 and API 35; verify both runs execute the production-bridge test and retain the unrelated-domain control cookie. No workflow edits are authorized unless this existing runner is proven not to execute the test.
- **Acceptance:** focused CookieBridge tests and the complete Third-category app JVM suite pass at exact HEAD; real production-bridge instrumentation passes on API 28 and API 35; exact run/job/head evidence and reports are recorded; no Fourth-category tests are run or modified.
- **Explicit exclusions:** production HTTP gateway/factory wiring; login UI; hidden WebView process/Service/Binder/IPC; SSL callback adapter/trust policy; Application/manifest; Reader/UI; `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.kt`; workflow/script changes unless separately preregistered; Fourth-category production source/tests/coordinator; PPRule; schema/migration; upstream pin; `main`.

#### Runtime-3.2e.4 source/caller audit — design blocker, no implementation

- **Audit HEAD:** `a9fc39400b36d637339dc4f3f818693b51a4fdcf`; no production or test source was modified and no CI was triggered.
- **Production HTTP authority is already present:** `BadcatReadingEngineFactory.create()` constructs one `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar` per factory graph and passes it to `OkHttpSourceRequestClient(cookieJarProvider = { sourceCookieStore })`. The same jar is exposed to Rhino CookieStore read/write/remove helpers. The resulting `SourceLoginSessionRequestClient` is passed into `BadcatSourceHttpGatewayFactory`, so ordinary search/explore/detail/TOC/content requests already use the authoritative jar when `BookSource.enabledCookieJar` enables it.
- **Request paths are broader than the gateway:** the `sourceAjax`, `sourceGet`, `sourceHttpRequest`, `sourceHttpRequestNoRedirectWithTimeout` and `sourceHttpRequestWithTimeout` Rhino callbacks in `BadcatReadingEngineFactory` call the same `durableRequestClient` directly. A decorator added only inside `BadcatSourceHttpGatewayFactory` would miss these JS request paths. Any future transport-wide integration must wrap the shared `SourceRequestClient` below both gateway and Rhino paths.
- **Existing HTTP cookie behavior:** `OkHttpSourceRequestClient.clientFor()` selects the host-owned `CookieJar` only when `request.useCookieJar` is true; otherwise it uses `NoSourceCookies`. Its `TrackingSourceCookieJar` captures the effective jar header, and `CookieHeaderMergeInterceptor` merges explicit request/login Cookie headers with jar values, with the jar winning same-name conflicts. Response Set-Cookie is saved through the same selected jar. `SourceLoginSessionRequestClient` adds saved login headers only when the target URL matches the source's effective registrable domain. The current persistent/session cookie authority is therefore the existing jar, not the WebView provider.
- **Actual source/login callers found:** `SourceSearchActivity`, `SourceBookActivity` and `SourceCatalogActivity` construct `BadcatReadingEngineFactory` graphs; `SourceCatalogActivity` and `SourceLoginUiV2Activity` also directly read/clear the same SharedPreferences cookie authority. Login UI v2 is a native declarative form executed by `LegadoSourceLoginUiV2Service`; its Rhino runtime reads the shared cookie jar but does not host a WebView or expose a WebView login-completion callback.
- **WebView caller qualification:** the only app WebView callsite found in this source area is the Badcat chapter reader's HTML rendering WebView in `SourceBookActivity` / `SourceChapterActivity`. It loads the reader document, disables JavaScript and DOM storage, and calls `BadcatWebViewPurificationAdapter.onPageFinished` for the Badcat page-injection/purification path. This is not a book-source login/browser session and is explicitly outside this Third-category task. It must not be repurposed as a source login WebView or modified as a shortcut.
- **Bridge caller inventory:** `DefaultProcessCookieBridge`, `syncFromWebView`, `syncToWebView` and `invalidateDomain` have no production callers in the audited source tree. The Android `CookieManager` adapter is currently used only by the bridge and its instrumentation. The bridge therefore has no source-specific WebView lifecycle event from which to observe/import a just-authenticated session.
- **Why automatic wiring is unsafe:** importing `CookieManager.getCookie(url)` before every HTTP request would re-import stale WebView values into the session map and can shadow a newer HTTP Set-Cookie value. Exporting the jar to WebView after each response writes name/value pairs with `Path=/` and cannot remove stale WebView names absent from the jar; it would also populate the process-wide WebView provider without a source-WebView owner. Observing HTTP URLs alone does not create a source WebView lifecycle. Wiring only the gateway would also miss the direct Rhino request callbacks listed above. These approaches would introduce ambiguous cookie ownership and altered semantics, violating this registration's safety contract.
- **Logout/clear gap:** the existing source-catalog clear/delete actions call `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.removeCookie(source.id)` directly. They do not call `DefaultProcessCookieBridge.invalidateDomain`; a future source-WebView login host will need a source-aware logout lifecycle that fails closed across both stores. Do not silently claim WebView state is cleared today.
- **Decision:** do not modify the factory, request client, reader WebView or category-4 purification adapter to force bridge calls. The existing HTTP jar is already correctly shared across normal and JS HTTP request paths; the missing prerequisite is a real source-WebView/browser login host with explicit source identity, login completion, navigation URL observation and logout callbacks. Register that host/lifecycle as a separate bounded task first. Once it exists, integrate the bridge at the shared transport/composition boundary and the explicit WebView lifecycle boundary, with a production-graph test covering all HTTP entry points.
- **Files reviewed:** `BadcatReadingEngineFactory.kt`, `BadcatSourceHttpGatewayFactory.kt`, `DefaultProcessCookieBridge.kt`, `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.kt`, `SourceLoginSession.kt`, `RhinoSourceCookieExtensions.kt`, `LegadoSourceLoginUiV2Service.kt`, `SourceLoginUiV2Activity.kt`, `SourceCatalogActivity.kt`, `SourceSearchActivity.kt`, `SourceBookActivity.kt`, `BadcatPurificationCoordinator.kt`, `OkHttpSourceRequestClient.kt`, `SourceHttpGateway.kt`, `SourceRequestFactory.kt`, and `BadcatSourceHttpGatewayFactoryTest.kt`.
- **Self-review / exclusions:** branch remains `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`; no Reader/UI, AdMark/purification, manifest, service/process/IPC, HTTP semantics, cookie storage, schema, Fourth-category, PPRule or upstream files changed. No test/build was run because the result is an architecture stop decision, not a code change. This evidence-only update uses `[skip ci]`.


#### Runtime-3.2e.5 source WebView/browser login host prerequisite — preregistration

- **Date / category:** 2026-11-23; Category 3, Legado Runtime.

The existing HTTP CookieJar is already shared across gateway and direct Rhino HTTP paths; forcing CookieBridge sync into those paths would import stale WebView values or populate a process-wide provider without source ownership. The existing reader WebView is not a source login browser.
- **Goal:** perform a bounded upstream/host architecture audit for the minimum source-scoped WebView/browser login capability required by the pinned Legado book-source execution contract. Use typed source identity and lifecycle-scoped Host Ports. #### Runtime-3.2e.5 pinned-SHA WebView/browser host audit — evidence and decision

- **Audit HEAD:** `8e50a681b85e67ef9af807d23f11b4407699a2b8`; upstream source is read at exact `LegadoTeam/legado@330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`. No production source, tests, manifest, permissions or workflow were modified.
- **Upstream visible source-login path:** `SourceLoginActivity.initView` routes sources without a declarative login form to `WebViewLoginFragment` (`app/src/main/java/io/legado/app/ui/login/SourceLoginActivity.kt:26-32`). `SourceLoginViewModel` resolves the active BaseSource, book/source type, login header map and stored login info. The fragment acquires a pooled WebView, applies source headers/User-Agent, loads the resolved `loginUrl`, observes both `onPageStarted` and `onPageFinished`, reads `android.webkit.CookieManager.getCookie(url)`, and calls `CookieStore.setCookie(source.getKey(), cookie)`; when the user taps login-check it reloads the login URL and finishes after page completion (`WebViewLoginFragment.kt:80-110, 162-175`). It releases the pooled WebView on destruction.
- **Upstream CookieStore semantics are materially different from this host's bridge:** at the pinned SHA, `CookieStore.setCookie(url,cookie)` calls `saveCookie`, resolves the effective domain with `NetworkUtils.getSubDomain`, writes the full name/value header to `appDb.cookieDao`, and updates the domain cookie cache (`CookieStore.kt:26-38`). It does not preserve WebView Set-Cookie expiry/session attributes; WebView-visible pairs copied from login are persisted in the upstream CookieStore. Separately, HTTP `CookieManager.saveResponse` classifies parsed response cookies into persistent DB cookies and in-memory session cookies (`CookieManager.kt:24-43`). `CookieStore.getCookie` merges those stores (`CookieStore.kt:85-107`). `CookieStore.removeCookie` clears the database row, persistent/session cache entries and the Android WebView cookie for the supplied URL (`CookieStore.kt:110-116`).
- **Current host deviation:** `DefaultProcessCookieBridge.syncFromWebView` calls `SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.mergeWebViewCookieHeader`, which deliberately imports name/value pairs into the process-only session map and never writes them to SharedPreferences. This is safer against persisting unknown session cookies, but it is not equivalent to pinned upstream WebView-login `CookieStore.setCookie`. `syncToWebView` writes each value as `Path=/`; upstream `CookieManager.applyToWebView` clears WebView session cookies then writes the CookieStore header against the base URL (`CookieManager.kt:141-150`). Neither side currently has an accepted differential proof of equivalence.
- **Upstream background rule-WebView path:** `JsExtensions.webView/webViewGetSource/webViewGetOverrideUrl` create `BackstageWebView`. It acquires a pooled WebView on the main thread, binds callbacks to the supplied coroutine navigation context, has a default 60-second timeout, releases the view on cancellation/error/completion, and checks view ownership before processing callbacks (`JsExtensions.kt:279-376`; `BackstageWebView.kt:74-188`). Rule HTML can register the source object, `WebJsExtensions` and cache receiver. On page completion it asynchronously copies `CookieManager.getCookie(url)` into `CookieStore.setCookie(tag,cookie)` (`BackstageWebView.kt:113-145, 200-205, 229-231, 388-390`).
- **Upstream asynchronous JS bridge:** `WebJsExtensions.request` dispatches 16 named async operations, including `webViewAwait`, `webViewGetSourceAwait`, network, crypto and file operations. It runs in Activity `lifecycleScope`, stores result/error by callback ID, and calls `evaluateJavascript` to settle the JS promise (`WebJsExtensions.kt:49-168, 244-375`). This is not represented by the current host's synchronous bounded Rhino façade.
- **Interactive browser and captcha path:** `SourceLoginJsExtensions.showBrowser` opens `BottomWebViewDialog` with the source identity, book type, URL/HTML/preload JS and config (`SourceLoginJsExtensions.kt:64-80`). The dialog registers the WebJsExtensions/source/cache bridges, handles browser navigation and lifecycle, and its network interception reads WebView cookies and applies response Set-Cookie values through Android CookieManager (`BottomWebViewDialog.kt:943-962, 1182-1240, 1311-1326`). `SourceVerificationHelp` can launch either a verification-code activity or the interactive browser, waits for user completion (up to five minutes), coalesces compatible concurrent verification requests, and propagates cancellation/cleanup (`SourceVerificationHelp.kt:200-400`).
- **WebView pool/lifecycle:** upstream `WebViewPool` is a process-global pool. Release stops loading, removes all four JS interfaces, clears form/UI state, rehomes the context, loads a unique blank recycle URL, and only returns the view to the idle pool after a guarded completion callback; idle views are later destroyed (`WebViewPool.kt:20-180`). The Android CookieManager itself is process-wide and is not source-isolated by the pool. Source identity/domain isolation is implemented in CookieStore, not by separate WebView cookie managers.
- **SSL compatibility/security conflict:** pinned upstream login, BackstageWebView and browser callbacks call `SslErrorHandler.proceed()` on SSL errors (`WebViewLoginFragment.kt:141-146`, `BackstageWebView.kt:242-252, 397-405`, `BottomWebViewDialog.kt:1232-1238`). This is permissive and must not be copied into a new host without an explicit security decision and tests. Host HTTP transport currently uses OkHttp's default TLS validation; this is not equivalent to accepting arbitrary WebView certificate errors.
- **Current host gap:** native Login UI v2 renders declarative rows and stores login info; it does not implement the legacy `loginUrl` WebView fallback, WebView JS interfaces, background WebView rule evaluation, interactive browser, or verification/captcha host. The reader WebView is local chapter HTML with JavaScript/DOM storage disabled and Badcat purification callbacks; it is not a source browser and must not be repurposed. Current host audits 1.6–1.8 remain static metadata/source audits, not end-to-end Android source-WebView parity evidence.
- **GO/NO-GO:** **GO** for a new, source-scoped typed Android Host Port and additive Badcat login/browser host; **NO-GO** for directly wiring the current CookieBridge into every HTTP request, reusing the reader WebView, or claiming upstream WebView compatibility. Implementation must include explicit source identity, navigation and login completion, cancellation, callback ownership, resource release, CookieManager synchronization and scoped logout. Background rule-WebView, interactive browser/captcha and WebView JS bridge remain separate acceptance layers; do not represent the login-only host as full WebView parity.
- **Blocking decision before CookieBridge login import is changed:** pinned upstream persists WebView-login name/value pairs via `CookieStore.setCookie`; the current host intentionally imports them session-only. These behaviors conflict. The fixed-SHA compatibility rule points toward upstream persistence, while the current security boundary avoids persisting cookies whose attributes cannot be observed. No implementation may silently choose between them. Obtain an explicit project decision and add a differential contract test before changing this behavior.
- **Next bounded task:** register a cookie import persistence decision first. After that decision, register the additive source-login WebView host implementation with exact files, manifest entry, lifecycle and API 28/35 tests. The broader background rule-WebView/JS bridge and interactive browser/captcha host should be separate tasks.
- **Self-review:** reviewed the three existing host audits, pinned upstream login fragment/viewmodel, CookieStore and CookieManager, BackstageWebView, WebJsExtensions, SourceLoginJsExtensions, SourceVerificationHelp, WebViewPool, WebViewRequestConfig, BottomWebViewDialog and relevant tests; compared them with current host bridge, factory, login UI, source session and reader WebView. No CI was run because this is a read-only audit and its documentation record uses `[skip ci]`.

#### Runtime-3.2e.6 WebView Cookie 持久化策略决策与策略化导入 — preregistration

- **日期 / 分类：** 2026-11-23；第三类：Legado 运行时。
- **用户决策：** 用户明确选择方案 C（分层策略）。
- **决策状态：** 已决定；本节同时登记下一项实现任务。注册提交不包含生产代码。
- **起始 HEAD：** `0eee49982e3ba41af8d4627527bc4c56ca5b9ff7`；分支：`integration/legado-upstream-runtime`；固定上游：`LegadoTeam/legado@330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`。
- **正式策略：**
  1. `LEGADO_COMPAT` 是默认策略。显式源登录/WebView 完成时，将 CookieManager 可见的 name/value 对按固定 SHA 的 `CookieStore.setCookie` 兼容语义写入持久化 Cookie 域桶；进程重启后仍可读取。
  2. `SESSION_ONLY` 是可选策略。相同导入只进入进程内 session map，进程重启后消失，不提升为磁盘持久化。
  3. HTTP 响应 `Set-Cookie` 的现有持久/会话分类、过期处理和同名覆盖规则保持不变。
  4. 每次 WebView 导入记录稳定来源身份的不可逆摘要、有效域、策略和导入时间；元数据不得包含 Cookie 名称/值、完整 Cookie Header、认证头或其他秘密。原始来源标识不得为了审计而新增明文持久化。
  5. `LEGADO_COMPAT` 的持久化只承诺与上游 WebView-login 的 name/value 持久化行为对齐；CookieManager 不暴露原始 `Expires`/`Max-Age` 等属性，不能声称保留或还原浏览器原始过期语义。
  6. 策略只在显式 source-WebView 生命周期回调中应用；禁止每次 HTTP 请求前自动导入 WebView Cookie，禁止跨来源推断身份，禁止全局 Cookie 清空。
- **上游差异依据：** 固定 SHA 的 `WebViewLoginFragment` 与 `BackstageWebView` 在页面完成后读取 `CookieManager.getCookie(url)` 并调用 `CookieStore.setCookie(sourceKey, cookie)`；`CookieStore.setCookie` 将可见 name/value header 写入持久化 CookieDao。当前 Badcat `mergeWebViewCookieHeader` 则只写进程 session map，属于已确认的兼容差异。HTTP `CookieManager.saveResponse` 对服务端 Cookie 仍区分持久与 session，不能把两种来源混为一谈。
- **允许修改的生产文件：**
  - `app/src/main/java/app/badcat/client/runtime/SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJar.kt`：增加明确的 WebView 导入策略分支和不含 Cookie 明文的导入元数据读写；保持 HTTP CookieJar 路径语义。
  - `app/src/main/java/app/badcat/client/runtime/DefaultProcessCookieBridge.kt`：为显式导入 API 增加必需的稳定 source identity 与策略参数，默认 `LEGADO_COMPAT`；不添加 HTTP 请求前自动同步。
- **允许修改的测试文件：**
  - `app/src/test/kotlin/app/badcat/client/runtime/SharedPreferencesSourceCookieJarTest.kt`
  - `app/src/test/kotlin/app/badcat/client/runtime/DefaultProcessCookieBridgeTest.kt`
- **实现要求：**
  - 以枚举/封闭类型表达 `LEGADO_COMPAT` 与 `SESSION_ONLY`，不得使用字符串魔法值或 Any/Map 通用桥接。
  - `LEGADO_COMPAT` 必须通过进程重建测试；并用固定上游语义测试证明导入结果、持久化覆盖/合并边界及同名优先级。不得只把现有 session-only 测试改成通过而不验证持久化。
  - `SESSION_ONLY` 必须验证同进程可见、重建 session store 后不可见，且不会写入持久化区。
  - 元数据必须按 source identity + effective domain 隔离；验证来源摘要稳定、不同来源隔离、策略与时间准确、Cookie 明文/头部不出现在元数据中；域清理必须一并清理该域元数据。
  - HTTP persistent/session response-cookie 分类、删除/过期行为和现有请求读取行为不得回归。
  - WebView 导入必须显式带 source identity；空/非法来源身份、非法 URL、超长 Header 和无有效 name/value 对均 fail closed；不记录 Cookie 值。
- **验收：** 两个指定 JVM 测试文件通过；完整第三类 App JVM suite 在 exact HEAD CI 通过；检查 diff 确认没有第四类、Reader/UI、manifest、HTTP factory、隐藏进程/IPC、SSL 策略或 schema 改动。若策略引入的存储边界无法证明，停止并记录阻断，不得降级为无来源身份导入。
- **明确排除：** source-WebView 登录界面/Host Port；Application/manifest/权限；WebView 生命周期和 CookieBridge 生产调用接线；后台规则 WebView、JS bridge、交互浏览器/验证码；HTTP gateway/factory；SSL 回调与证书策略；Reader/UI；第四类 AdMark/AdBlock；第五类 PPRule；数据库 schema 迁移；上游 pin；`main`。
- **后续顺序：** 本任务通过后，再独立登记 source-scoped login WebView host，将来源身份、登录完成、Cookie 导入/导出、登出失效和生命周期接入；背景规则 WebView/JS bridge 与交互浏览器/验证码继续分项登记。
- **状态：** 已注册，尚未实施；注册文档提交使用 `[skip ci]`。

#### Runtime-3.2f.2 AnalyzeUrl retry default parity — preregistration

- **日期 / 分类：** 2026-11-23；第三类：Legado 运行时。
- **起始 HEAD：** `290ad69094159e14115f46a391a977917ac4bea6`；分支 `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`；固定上游 SHA `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`。

- **目标：** 缺少 `retry` 时解析为 `0`；显式 `retry:0` 仍为 `0`；显式正整数原样保留；非法/负数/超上限仍 fail closed。不得改变 IOException/HTTP 状态可重试判定、延迟、最大值或非幂等请求保护。
- **允许修改文件：**
  - `integration-contract/src/main/kotlin/app/badcat/engine/LegadoUrlResolver.kt`
  - `integration-contract/src/test/kotlin/app/badcat/engine/LegadoUrlResolverTest.kt`
  - `integration-contract/src/test/kotlin/app/badcat/engine/SourceRequestFactoryTest.kt`
- **测试要求：** 更新默认 retry 契约断言为 0；保留显式 0/正数测试；增加从 URL resolver 产物经 `SourceRequestFactory` 传递到 `SourceHttpRequest.retryCount` 的默认值验证；既有上限和显式配置测试继续通过。
- **验收：** `:integration-contract:test` 通过；完整第三类 App JVM suite 在 exact implementation SHA CI 通过；diff 仅限上述三个文件；核对上游固定 SHA 与 caller 传递链；不得把正在执行的 #3157 结果借用为本任务通过证据。

- **并行安全：** 与 Runtime-3.2f.1 的 codec 文件范围完全不重叠，且无共享可变状态；可在 #3157 仍运行时独立实施。分支更新须使用 expected SHA/CAS。

#### Runtime-3.2f.7 AnalyzeUrl boolean option parity — preregistration

- **日期 / 分类：** 2026-11-23；第三类：Legado 运行时 URL / HTTP request options。
- **起始 HEAD：** `2ffc89196263d4238d749876ab333178b308fab4`；分支 `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`；固定上游 SHA `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`。
- **源码依据：** 固定 SHA `AnalyzeUrl.kt` 的 `UrlOption.useWebView()` 仅将 `null`、空字符串、Boolean false、字符串 `"false"` 判为 false，其余值为 true；`getFollowRedirects()` 调用 `parseBooleanOption`，后者只接受 Boolean、数值精确等于 0.0/1.0、字符串 true/false/1/0，其余返回 null。
- **发现：** 当前 resolver 共用 `booleanValue` 处理两个不同语义字段；followRedirects 的显式 null 被转换成 false，数值 0.5/1.5 经 `asInt` 可能被截断，webView 的字符串 `"0"` / 数值 0 被当作 false，且其他非空值直接报错。这与固定上游两个字段的不同转换规则不一致。
- **目标：** 分离两个字段的解析规则。followRedirects：missing/null/无效类型返回 null；Boolean 原值；Number 仅 0.0/1.0 有效；字符串按 trim + lowercase 接受 true/1/false/0，其他返回 null。webView：严格复刻固定上游 false 集合（null、空字符串、Boolean false、精确小写字符串 `"false"`）；其余值表示 true，随后按既有规则因当前宿主未实现 WebView URL option 而返回 UNSUPPORTED_RULE。
- **允许修改文件：**
  - `integration-contract/src/main/kotlin/app/badcat/engine/LegadoUrlResolver.kt`
  - `integration-contract/src/test/kotlin/app/badcat/engine/LegadoUrlResolverTest.kt`
- **调用链：** URL option JSON → resolver `followRedirects` / `webView` → `LegadoResolvedUrl.followRedirects` → `SourceRequestFactory` → `SourceHttpRequest.followRedirects` → OkHttp client redirect policy。
- **测试要求：** followRedirects Boolean、整数/整值小数 0/1、0.5/1.5、null、合法字符串、无效字符串；webView null/empty/false/"false" 与 0/"0"/"true"/true/其他非空值；确认 true 最终 fail closed 为 UNSUPPORTED_RULE，且 false 不触发 WebView。
- **验收：** focused `:integration-contract:test` 与完整第三类 App JVM suite 在 exact implementation SHA CI 通过；diff 仅限上述两个文件；确认与固定 SHA 上游转换逻辑逐项一致；不得借用 #3160/#3162 的 CI 结果。
- **排除：** HTTP redirect transport 实现、安全策略、retry/timeout/charset、WebView host implementation、Cookie/login、JS ABI、source UI、第四/第五类、上游 pin、`main`。
- **依赖与并行：** 与 #3160 同一 resolver 文件范围重叠；必须等 #3160 终态并完成清单回写后才可实施。#3162 文件范围不重叠。
- **状态：** 实现已提交（`b0fcd0621ab8391cfa451cfbd663b2505b84fe57`）；CI #3165 in progress，等待 exact-HEAD 验证。

### Runtime-3.2f.10 TOC duplicate-URL chapter preservation — preregistration

- **日期 / 分类：** 2026-11-23；第三类：Legado TOC merge / chapter identity.
- **起始 HEAD：** `78b91b77fe62e4d314d539e798b03e9a3387de55`；分支 `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`；固定上游 `LegadoTeam/legado@330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`。
- **已核实差异：** Badcat `SourceTocService.load` 在增量回调和最终返回两处都使用 `distinctBy { it.url }`，会把同 URL、不同标题/元数据的合法章节合并掉。固定上游 `BookChapterList.analyzeChapterList` 使用 `LinkedHashSet(chapterList)`，依据完整章节对象相等性稳定去重；固定上游 `BookChapter` 是 data class，URL 不是唯一身份。上游 `BatchContentContext` 明确允许同 URL 多章节，并要求 URL 回传存在歧义时拒绝解析。
- **上游证据路径：**
  - `app/src/main/java/io/legado/app/model/webBook/BookChapterList.kt`（固定 SHA；TOC merge 使用 LinkedHashSet）
  - `app/src/main/java/io/legado/app/data/entities/BookChapter.kt`（固定 SHA；data class 字段与对象相等性）
  - `app/src/main/java/io/legado/app/model/BatchContentContext.kt`（固定 SHA；重复 URL 身份约定）
  - `app/src/test/java/io/legado/app/model/BatchContentContextTest.kt`（固定 SHA；重复 URL 与 ambiguity 契约）
- **Badcat callers：** `SourceTocService.load` 的增量 `onChapters` 与最终 `EngineResult.Success<List<BookChapter>>`；调用者 `SourceReadingEngine.chaptersIncrementalWithFallback`、`SourceBookActivity.showChapters/loadBook`。本任务不改变调用者 UI。
- **目标：** 两处合并均改为按当前 host `BookChapter` 投影的 data-class equality 稳定去重；保留 URL 相同但 title、VIP/pay 或 tag 不同的章节；只折叠当前投影字段完全相等的重复记录；最终按合并顺序重新分配 index。明确记录 host 投影不含 upstream BookChapter 全部字段，因此本任务只承诺当前投影可见字段的等价性，不声称完整模型 equality 已覆盖。
- **允许修改文件：**

#### Runtime-3.2f.11 chapter URL alias normalization — audit result

- **审计 HEAD：** `123f1e5476d5ffd26be54be317f46092fcf6f92d`；固定上游 `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`。报告：`docs/audits/legado-runtime-3.2f.11-chapter-url-alias-differential.md`。
- **已核实：** 固定上游 `BookChapter.getAbsoluteURL` 先处理卷章节，再用 `AnalyzeUrl.paramPattern = \\s*,\\s*(?=\\{)` 拆分逗号 options suffix；URL 前缀由 `NetworkUtils.getAbsoluteURL` 解析并在返回时重新拼接 options。上游 `NetworkUtils` 使用 `java.net.URL(base, relative)`，有 null/invalid base、HTTP(S)、data URL 和 javascript 特殊分支。BatchContentContext 的 URL 索引同时保存原始 URL、chapter.getAbsoluteURL() 和基于 `book.tocUrl.ifBlank { bookSource.bookSourceUrl }` 的 normalize URL；输入先 trim，原始命中与 normalize 命中合并后按 chapter.index 去重，只允许唯一候选。章节对象按 index 解析，数字标识拒绝。
- **Badcat 差异：** `ChapterCatalogQuery.findByUrl` 仅做字符串精确相等；`findByIdentity` 仅以 index 定位并用原始 URL 精确校验，没有 base URL 或 alias normalize。Host `BookChapter` 没有 upstream `baseUrl/isVolume` 等字段。SourceBookActivity 的续读按钮、开始阅读续读及 URL-only reader launch 都走 URL 查找；BookmarkActivity/ReadingHistoryActivity 仍只传 chapterUrl/title，不传 index；BadcatReadingStateRepository 的 last chapter/bookmark/history 记录也未保存 TOC base URL 或 chapter index。
- **关键风险：** 上游 `BookChapter.getAbsoluteURL` 的 base 是每章 `chapter.baseUrl`，而 BatchContentContext.normalize 的 base 是 `book.tocUrl`（空时退回 source URL）；分页目录中的每章 base 可能不同。当前 host parser 已将章节链接解析为绝对 URL，但没有保留每章响应 finalUrl/baseUrl，因此仅给 `findByUrl` 增加一个 book-level baseUrl 参数，不能证明所有分页相对 URL 与逗号 options 的等价性。URL 归一化仅用于身份匹配，不能绕过 WebUrlResolver 的 HTTP(S)/credential 安全限制。
- **调用点证据：** `SourceBookActivity.kt` 中开始阅读和“继续上次阅读”按钮的 URL 恢复、`SourceChapterActivity.loadInitial` 的 URL-only 旧 intent 解析；`BookmarkActivity.kt`、`ReadingHistoryActivity.kt` 发出的 intent 仅包含 URL/title；`BadcatReadingStateRepository.kt` 的持久化 key 以 sourceId/bookUrl/chapterUrl 编码。代码搜索接口没有返回可用完整索引，因此报告只声明上述直接静态确认的调用点，不宣称形式化全仓 call graph。
- **测试矩阵建议：** chapter-specific base URL、TOC base fallback、分页 redirect finalUrl、relative/absolute/protocol-relative、dot segments、query/fragment、options suffix 空白与 JSON、HTTP(S)大小写、data/javascript、invalid base fallback、同 alias 多 chapter、同 URL twins、chapter object/index identity、数字/空/未知标识、旧 URL-only bookmark/history。所有未由上游源码或固定样本证明的边界保持 unresolved。
- **GO/NO-GO：** **GO** 进入单独的 host chapter-baseUrl 投影与纯 JVM differential fixture 设计；**NO-GO** 直接修改当前 `ChapterCatalogQuery` 并宣称上游 alias parity。需要先明确每章 baseUrl 如何从 TOC parser 传到 catalog、旧 URL-only 记录如何安全恢复，以及 duplicate URL 时是否必须继续 fail closed。后续生产实现须另行 preregister，且依赖 .10 的 exact-SHA 验收结论。
- **实际范围：** 仅新增审计报告并更新本清单；无生产代码、测试、Gradle、workflow、数据库、UI/Reader 或 `main` 修改。只读审计未运行构建/测试/CI。
- **状态：** 审计结果已完成；alias normalization 实现仍未登记/未通过；BatchContentContext 生产 JS/rule 双路径仍未接入，继续作为第三类阻断项。

### Runtime-3.2f.12 cache mutation callers and invalidation closure — audit result

- **审计 HEAD：** 136819704e6fd508e2889195d5ae0f591c6dacc3；固定上游 LegadoTeam/legado@330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a。报告：docs/audits/legado-runtime-3.2f.12-cache-mutation-invalidation-audit.md。
- **上游 caller 盘点：** 固定 SHA 的 GitHub code search 对 CacheManager 返回 43 个文件且 incomplete_results=false；另对 delContent 返回 11 个文件、saveText 17 个、reverseContent 9 个、commitResources 2 个。结果按 CacheManager/WebCacheManager/AppCacheManager/AudioCacheManager 分域；Audio/RSS/视频媒体缓存不冒充书源 runtime 缓存。
- **上游机制：** CacheManager 的 string cache 是 Room caches 表 + 内存 LRU；saveTime 单位秒，TTL 写入 DB 后会清掉同 key 内存值，永久值才提升进内存；delete 同时删 DB、内存与 ACache 文件。putFile/getFile/ByteArray 由 ACache 提供。App 启动时 CacheDao.clearDeadline(now) 清理过期 DB 项。BaseSource 把 loginHeader/userInfo/sourceVariable/v_ 等状态写入不同 key 前缀；source 删除清理只覆盖 CacheDao 的 v_ 与 sourceVariable_ 前缀，不等于全 CacheManager namespace 清空。
- **上游正文写入：** BookHelp.ContentSaveFence 用 bookUrl+chapterIndex 做 key，token 包含 folderName/version；同步 fence 对 saveContent 做版本校验，saveText/reverseContent/commitResources/delContent 通过 replace 先提升版本再写/删。ReadBookViewModel、ContentEditDialog、ReadBookActivity、ChangeChapterSourceViewModel、ResourceRefresh 等是正文 mutation callers；ReadBookViewModel 的删除路径还调用独立 CacheBook.invalidateChapters。BatchContentContext 捕获每章 save token 并调用 BookHelp.saveContent，与通用 CacheManager 是不同机制。
- **Badcat 正文缓存发现：** SourceChapterContentService 在网络前 beginSave，读取 index-key cache，成功后缓存经过 scoped text replacement 的最终正文；默认 TTL 12 小时。File cache 使用 AtomicFile、全局文件 Mutex、64 MiB LRU prune，另有 legacy URL-key get/put 与 index-key fenced get/put 两个命名空间。expired 文件只在读取时判定过期，不立即删除，主要由 LRU 回收。
- **正文缓存阻断：** ChapterContentSaveFence 内部普通 HashMap 已由 token/isCurrent/publishIfCurrent/replace/invalidate 上的 @Synchronized 保护，同一实例内是线程安全的；beginSave/isCurrent 不受文件 Mutex 保护，但受 fence 自身实例 monitor 保护。真正的问题是 fence 在每个 FileChapterContentCache 实例内创建，每个实例有独立 map/monitor；BadcatReadingEngineFactory.create() 每次构建新 cache，因此多个 engine 实例共享文件 Mutex，却不共享 fence generation，跨实例旧请求可能在新实例 invalidate 后仍发布。接口虽暴露 invalidate(sourceId,bookUrl,index)，但当前 SourceChapterContentService 没有 mutation/invalidation caller；本次检查到的 SourceBookActivity/SourceCatalogActivity 删除书源流程也没有章节缓存 clear/invalidate。index invalidate 不删除 legacy URL-key 文件。
- **正文测试缺口：** ChapterContentSaveFenceTest 仅验证同一 fence 的串行版本变化；SourceChapterContentServiceTest 使用 fake cache；FileChapterContentCacheTest 只覆盖 digest 与 bounded reader；没有真实 AtomicFile 写入/恢复/多实例 fence/TTL 清理/TOC refresh invalidation 的集成测试。
- **Badcat 通用 source cache：** RhinoSourceCacheExtensions 的 string KV 用 sourceId 隔离并在 JSON 中写 expiresAt；file cache 使用 AtomicFile、sourceId/key SHA-256 名称与 50 MiB 全局预算。RhinoSourceScriptRuntime.clearSourceState 会清除 memory、key-value、file cache、物理目录、登录 session 和 Cookie。差异：host cache.delete(key) 只删 KV，不删同 key 的 fileStore 项；host cache.clear() 清 memory/fileStore，但不清 KV；需要 runtime clearSourceState 才能清两类持久存储。SourceCatalogActivity 删除源只清 login session/Cookie；importJson 可按同 ID 替换源配置，当前 inspected callers 没有调用 clearSourceState。GitHub host code-search index 不完整，因此未把“没有任何其他调用点”当成事实。
- **GO/NO-GO：** NO-GO 声称正文缓存 fence/失效闭环与 upstream BookHelp 等价；NO-GO 声称 Rhino cache.delete/clear 与 upstream CacheManager.delete 语义等价。GO 进入独立实现任务设计：先做 process-wide、线程安全的 chapter fence + 真正的跨实例/AtomicFile instrumentation；再登记 source remove/replace 的 cache lifecycle hook 和 KV/file 双域 delete/clear 修正。不得一次性混入 UI、数据库迁移或其他类别。
- **范围核验：** 本审计仅新增报告与清单结果；未修改生产代码、测试、Gradle、workflow、数据库、UI/Reader 或 main；未运行构建、测试、CI、APK 或设备验证。
- **状态：** 审计已完成；实现项仍未登记/未通过。第三类 BatchContentContext 的 JS/rule 批量正文生产接线仍未完成。


### Runtime-3.2f.13 process-wide thread-safe chapter save fence — preregistration

- **日期 / 分类：** 2026-11-23；第三类：chapter content cache concurrency / stale-write fencing.
- **起始 HEAD：** `1ac35ff0dbcf097b03515347cf70f4db780ff111`；分支 `integration/legado-upstream-runtime`；固定上游 `LegadoTeam/legado@330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`。
- **依据：** Runtime-3.2f.12 audit confirmed `FileChapterContentCache` shares a process-wide file Mutex but constructs a per-instance `ChapterContentSaveFence`. The fence methods already use `@Synchronized`, protecting the plain HashMap within each instance; the gap is that each cache instance has a separate map/monitor. `BadcatReadingEngineFactory.create()` constructs a new cache instance each invocation. The pinned upstream `BookHelp.ContentSaveFence` also serializes state and write/replace operations.
- **目标：** make fence operations linearizable and thread-safe; use one process-wide fence instance for all FileChapterContentCache instances; preserve key identity `(sourceId,bookUrl,chapterIndex)`; preserve semantics that replace advances generation before running write and remains advanced even if write throws; a token captured by one engine must be rejected after another engine invalidates/replaces the same chapter.
- **允许修改文件：**
  - `integration-contract/src/main/kotlin/app/badcat/engine/ChapterContentSaveFence.kt`
  - `app/src/main/java/app/badcat/client/runtime/FileChapterContentCache.kt`
  - `integration-contract/src/test/kotlin/app/badcat/engine/ChapterContentSaveFenceTest.kt`
- **测试要求：** shared process-wide fence used by two logical cache instances; cross-instance stale token rejected; invalidate-before-publish rejects callback; publish/replace/invalidate are serialized under contention; concurrent token/invalidate operations do not corrupt state; failed replace still advances generation; invalidating one key leaves other source/book/chapter keys unchanged.
- **验收：** focused fence tests and complete third-category JVM suite pass on exact implementation SHA; CI compiles Android app and executes API 28/API 35 instrumentation; diff only touches the three registered files. Report the shared map's lifetime/memory tradeoff explicitly; do not claim disk invalidation callers were wired.
- **排除：** no new invalidate caller, source remove/reimport lifecycle, rule revision key, legacy URL cache cleanup, generic CacheManager delete/clear semantics, AtomicFile migration, BatchContentContext, UI/Reader, database/Room, fourth/fifth category, upstream pin or `main`.
- **并行与依赖：** based on .12 audit; file scope does not overlap #3167 test migration (`SourceTocServiceTest.kt`). #3167 remains independent and its CI result must not be reused.
- **风险：** process-wide version map may retain invalidated chapter keys for process lifetime; do not evict a generation while any in-flight token may still reference it. This task deliberately does not add token-release lifecycle.
- **状态：** 已登记，尚未实施；注册提交仅修改本清单并使用 `[skip ci]`。

### Runtime-3.2f.15 registration — source removal/replacement invalidates source-scoped runtime state

- **日期 / 分类：** 2026-11-23；第三类：BookSource mutation lifecycle / source-scoped Rhino state.
- **起始分支 / HEAD：** `integration/legado-upstream-runtime` / `370954cc9de3c3775200b027711ddaac211f3548`；固定上游 `330e606c4d57e08adc056ff8ab7a4132c784da9a`。
